question: Why do different one-hump maps share the same Feigenbaum number?
answer: Any single hump folds the line back the same way, so each split copies the last one. Because of this, the gaps between splits shrink by the same factor, 4.669, whatever the formula. Only the single hump matters, not the specific formula.
move: Only the single hump matters, not the formula: that is universality.
